source.title: The Central Bank Question
source.summary: What central banks actually do, why every country has one, and the fundamental tension with Islamic economics.
source.author: Islamic Economics
source.body_text: Central banks solved real problems: bank runs, credit crunches, currency instability. But they also created new ones: moral hazard, inflation bias, regressive distributional effects. This episode gives central banking an even-handed examination: what it does well, where it fails, and what the bayt al-mal as an Islamic monetary authority might look like. Turkey's inflation crisis illustrates what happens when central bank independence is compromised. The fundamental tension: Islamic economics prohibits interest rates, but modern central banking runs entirely on them. Can that circle be squared?

thread: Renaissance merchants needed no central bank. Their trade bills cleared across continents without anyone manipulating prices.
Central banks prevent bank runs and currency crises. They also create moral hazard and inflation bias. Every solution becomes a new problem.
Islamic economics faces a fundamental tension: it prohibits interest rates entirely. But modern central banking runs on nothing else.
Turkey's inflation hit 85% when politicians compromised central bank independence. The bayt al-mal offers a different monetary model. Listen: https://islamiceconomics.github.io/podcast.html#ep-mm-2

short_video.title: Why Islamic Economics Clashes with Central Banking
short_video.hook: Every country has a central bank. Islamic economics says they shouldn't exist.
short_video.voiceover: Central banks solved real problems: bank runs, credit crunches, currency crashes. But they created new ones: moral hazard, inflation bias, wealth concentration. Islamic economics prohibits interest rates entirely. Modern central banking runs on nothing else. Turkey's inflation hit eighty-five percent when politicians took over monetary policy. The bayt al-mal offers a different model: Islamic monetary authority without interest manipulation. Renaissance merchants cleared transactions across continents without central banks. Maybe we're solving the wrong problems.
